From the crushing depths to the salt-strewn air, competition has bred innovative adaptions for corals and flora to spread across every 
inch of the shifting landscape. Exposed to the sun and wind, the coral that rises from the tide tends to be hardier than their aquatic kin. 
Flexible bone-like plates grow along the bridging structures and can be carved away to be fashioned into a sturdy material for armor, 
the living plate rejuvenating itself in the salted waters of the ocean. Beyond the shore, wide swathes of kelp forests stretch along the 
shallows, their roots lit by the cold glow of deep dawn plants. Among these forests, seaweave grass grows in the light of those lit orbs, 
their dark green tough fibers though difficult to cut, make for an incredibly supple and durable material akin to boiled leather.
